Core behavior matches the reference on reading. on_key handling (tabs.py:295-329) covers Escape, arrows, digits, and first-character search. Click metadata is attached to inactive labels (tabs.py:~ inactive piece) and to the bar (underline_bar.py:96-99). Opacity now keeps non-color attributes such as meta (opacity.py:41), which is the intent.
Failure 1: the demo does not start. sandbox/tabs_demo.py:10 'await self.mount' against synchronous app.py:298 raises TypeError, so the sandbox artifact the reference delivers is broken.

Failure 2: the underline lands on the wrong tab when a duplicate name precedes the active one. The watcher (tabs.py:277) and __init__ (tabs.py:271) pass a full-list index from find_tab_by_name (tabs.py:381-388, iterating self.tabs). __rich_console__ treats that value as an index into displayed tabs with modulo wrapping (tabs.py:171-173). For tabs [A('x'), B('x'), C('y')], activating 'y' draws the underline under 'x'. The docstring at tabs.py:74 defines bar_position over displayed tabs, so the patch contradicts itself.

Reference comparison for failure 2: reference get_underline_bar indexes range_values[tab_index] with tab_index=2 on a list of length 2, which raises IndexError on the same input. The reference is also wrong here, but it fails loudly while the patch fails silently.
criteria.deficiency: Two intended behaviors fail: the sandbox demo crashes on startup (sandbox/tabs_demo.py:10 awaits synchronous App.mount at app.py:298), and the active-tab underline is misplaced when a duplicate name precedes the active tab (tabs.py:171-173 vs tabs.py:277 and tabs.py:381-388). The second is an edge case that the reference also mishandles, by crashing instead.
